recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-15660; future edits to the unit extension definitions should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack unless a new tracker asks for core narrative or terminology changes.
issue_request: FHIR-15660 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Questionnaire issue raised against STU3. It requested support for forms that let users choose among units for numeric answers and resolved to clarify questionnaire-unit as integer/decimal extraction guidance while adding extensions for quantity unit choices.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git commit 6ad07d308d7e7e08a07ee5d136f849941d01ab7d, matching Jira's svn revision 13425 comment. That commit updated the old core Questionnaire extensions spreadsheet to clarify questionnaire-unit and add unit-option and unit-valueSet rows for quantity items.
additional_context: Later source rework carried the seed change forward as questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet. Core commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 intentionally removed Questionnaire extension StructureDefinitions from R5 core source, and the Extension Pack now owns the authoritative definitions. Later related issues FHIR-20394, FHIR-34391, FHIR-37363, and FHIR-28132 refined the same unit-extension family and are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope core source points quantity items to questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet, decimal/integer items to questionnaire-unit, and the Extension Pack definitions contain the requested constraints and definitions.
